newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian top stocks post gains in upbeat trade.
newsitem.headline: Croatian top stocks post gains in upbeat trade.

text.p: Croatia's top shares posted new gains in upbeat trade on Wednesday and brokers said they expected market activity and prices to remain at current levels in the near future.
"I can't see any special developments...neither strong gains nor losses," said Hrvoje Bujanovic of IB Austria.
"But if the dollar rises again, (drugs firm) Pliva and Zagrebacka (Banka) could break new records," he said.

The two stocks accounted for three quarters of the total trade, Bujanovic said, adding their Zagreb prices were pushed up by a rise in their Global Depository Receipts (GDRs) which trade in U.S. dollars in London.
Drugs firm Pliva, selling 8,429 shares, was the most active stock. It rose 17.10 kuna to 525.10 and its GDRs fetched $16.5 in London, after opening at $16.25.
Zagrebacka ordinaries climbed 45 kuna to 2,205 on volume of 3,762 shares. The bank's GDRs traded at $34.7, up from $34.375 at the opening.
"There has been no fresh information on either of the firms that could have prompted their growth. I would say it is a simple conversion of currencies," Bujanovic said.

Pliva and Zagrebacka were among nine issues that rose in Zagreb on Wednesday, while three fell and three were flat. Volume was slightly lower at 30,163 units and turnover shrank to 16.9 million from 28.7 million kuna.
Top gainer ship repairer Viktor Lenac, which was fully listed last week in the top segment of the bourse, added 15.10 kuna or 9.7 percent to 171.1 kuna on volume of 6,619 shares.
Food processor Podravka edged up seven kuna to 249, with 5,742 units sold. Traders said the firm would not fall below 240 kuna, which proved to be its resistance point in the past weeks.
Hotelier Riviera Porec was also among gainers, adding five kuna to 157 and selling 1,208 shares.
Biggest decliner hotelier Zlatni Rat lost 10 kuna or 6.7 percent to 140 with 90 shares sold in a first deal since April.
